I am seventy-eight years old, and I have farmed these fields in Quzhou County since I was a boy. I only finished primary school, but I know this land better than any book. Last October I planted winter wheat on my six mu, the same plot I have always used. I bought improved wheat seed from the county supply shop and used the rotary tiller before sowing, just like every year. I put down about one big bag of compound fertilizer per mu as basal dressing — the shop sells a special blend that everyone around here uses.

Now it is spring, and the wheat is waking up. I will go out soon to topdress with urea when the wheat starts jointing, about half a bag per mu. My neighbor Lao Zhang does about the same, and his wheat always looks good. I will irrigate four times in total for this wheat crop: I already did the winter irrigation, and now I will water at green-up, at jointing, and when the heads are flowering. The electric pump costs money, but if I skip watering the yield will drop, and I cannot afford that. I will spray pesticides three times — once for weeds, once for insects when the weather warms, and a third time only if I see disease. I expect about 450 kilograms per mu if the weather behaves, which is about what I got last year.

Right after I harvest the wheat in early June, I will plant summer maize the same week. There is no time to plough — the window is only a few days — so I plant directly into the wheat stubble with no-tillage. I always buy hybrid maize seed, usually Nongda or Denghai varieties from the shop, about three jin per mu. I spread compound fertilizer at planting and topdress with urea once at the big-flare stage if the plants look yellow. I will irrigate maize twice: once after planting if the rains don't come, and once when the tassels appear. Two sprays for pests and weeds should be enough. I expect around 500 kilograms per mu.

I do not try new crops or fancy methods at my age. Wheat and maize have fed my family and paid for my grandchildren's school fees for decades. My son helps with the heavy lifting and the machine work now, but I make the decisions. I watch what the successful farmers in the village do, and I do the same. Change is risky, and I have seen too many bad years to gamble.
